skill.name: database
skill.description: Provides SQLModel and SQLAlchemy guidance for async connections, schema design, repositories, migrations, query optimization, and database testing across PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite.
skill.summary: Design and review Python database layers with practical SQLModel and SQLAlchemy patterns.
skill.author: Azeem-2

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives caused by SQLModel Session.exec and Markdown fences; they do not invoke Python, processes, or shells. The production example retains a default database credential, and generic repository writes accept unrestricted model fields.

remediation.issue: The production connection URL has a predictable credential fallback.
remediation.suggestion: Require DATABASE_URL in production and stop startup when it is missing. Keep placeholder credentials outside production configuration.

remediation.issue: Generic create and update methods allow unrestricted model fields.
remediation.suggestion: Use typed input schemas and explicit field allowlists. Reject changes to identifiers, ownership, privilege, and audit fields.

content.value_statement: Database layers often suffer from inconsistent sessions, schemas, and query patterns. This skill provides reusable SQLModel and SQLAlchemy examples for connections, repositories, migrations, optimization, and tests.
actual_capabilities: Design SQLModel models with indexes, relationships, timestamps, and soft deletion.
Configure asynchronous database engines, sessions, pooling, and cleanup.
Draft reusable repository methods for create, read, update, delete, filtering, and pagination.
Create Alembic migration patterns for tables, constraints, indexes, and rollback steps.
Review query performance, PostgreSQL statistics, and isolated database tests.
limitations: It provides documentation and examples; it does not connect to databases or execute migrations.
Some repository examples declare asynchronous functions while using synchronous Session methods.
PostgreSQL monitoring examples require pg_stat_statements and adaptation for current SQLAlchemy APIs.
Generated patterns still require schema-specific validation, authorization, load testing, and operational review.

use_cases.title: Create an application data layer
use_cases.description: Define models, sessions, repositories, and indexes for a new Python service.

use_cases.title: Review production database design
use_cases.description: Assess pooling, migrations, query plans, and PostgreSQL monitoring before deployment.

use_cases.title: Build isolated database tests
use_cases.description: Create fixtures and test cases for transactions, repositories, pagination, and tenant boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Create a starter schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Design SQLModel models for [domain]. Include field types, relationships, constraints, and essential indexes. Explain each design choice.

prompt_templates.title: Build an async repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an AsyncSession repository for [model]. Include typed create and update inputs, pagination, transactions, rollback, and an explicit field allowlist.

prompt_templates.title: Review a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this migration plan for [change]. Identify locking, data loss, rollback, index, and deployment risks. Propose safer steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit performance and isolation
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this database design for [workload]. Analyze query plans, pool sizing, tenant isolation, authorization boundaries, monitoring, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: Review a task repository that lists records by owner and supports pagination.
output: Finding: owner scoping is applied before optional filters.
Recommendation: cap page size and use typed filter fields.
Tests: verify cross-owner isolation, empty pages, and invalid limits.

output_examples.input: Plan a migration that adds a required status field to a large table.
output: Phase 1: add the nullable field without a table-wide default.
Phase 2: backfill records in monitored batches.
Phase 3: validate values, add the constraint, and define rollback.

best_practices: Use typed create and update schemas with explicit field allowlists.
Require production connection URLs through secret management and fail when configuration is missing.
Test transactions, tenant isolation, migrations, and query plans before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder credentials into production configurations.
Do not pass untrusted dictionaries directly into generic repository methods.
Do not mix synchronous session calls with asynchronous engines and request handlers.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to my database?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for your agent to adapt within your project.

faq.question: Which databases are covered?
faq.answer: The patterns target PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite through SQLModel and SQLAlchemy.

faq.question: Can I use the examples unchanged in production?
faq.answer: No. Validate session APIs, credentials, authorization, schema rules, and operational settings for your environment.

faq.question: Can it help create migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft Alembic migration structures, indexes, constraints, upgrade steps, and rollback plans.

faq.question: How should database secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Store them in an approved secret manager or protected environment variable. Production startup should fail when they are absent.

faq.question: Does it support asynchronous applications?
faq.answer: Yes. Review each example for consistent AsyncSession types and awaited methods before integration.
